chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated, he said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Arzami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Ali (peace be upon him) had a slave named Qanbar, who loved Ali (peace be upon him) with a strong love. Whenever Ali (peace be upon him) went out, Qanbar would go out behind him with a sword. So Ali (peace be upon him) saw him one night and said: 'O Qanbar, what is it?' He replied: 'I came to walk behind you, for people are as you see them, O Commander of the Faithful, so I feared for you.' He said: 'Woe to you! Are you guarding me from the inhabitants of the heaven or from the inhabitants of the earth?' He answered: 'No, but from the inhabitants of the earth.' He said: 'Verily, the inhabitants of the earth cannot do anything to me except by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and High, from the heaven. So go back,' and he returned.

key_terms.قَنْبَرُ: Qanbar, the slave of Imam Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali (AS) say about the people of the earth's ability to affect him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the practical piety of Qanbar, Ali’s (AS) devoted slave, whose vigilance against earthly threats prompted a theological clarification from Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The dialogue underscores the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Af'al* (Oneness of Divine Action), illustrating that while human agency exists, ultimate protection and decree are solely from God, rendering earthly forces powerless without His permission.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. My father said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ja`far ibn basher, on the authority of al-Arzami that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

`Ali (AS) had a slave called Qanbar, who loved his mater `Ali (AS) very much. When `Ali (AS) used to go out, Qanbar would go out behind him with a sword. So `Ali (AS) saw him one night, and asked him, “O Qanbar, what is it?” He replied, “I walk behind you because I know how people are, and I feared for you, O Commander of the Faithful.” The Imam (AS) questioned, “Woe to you! Are you guarding me from the inhabitants of the heaven or the earth?” He answered, “No, only from the inhabitants of the earth.” `Ali (AS) said: “Verily, the inhabitants of the earth cannot do anything against me except by the will of Allah, the Mighty and High, from Heaven. So go back.” Thus, he returned.
